cohort: The study included 49 pregnant patients who had percutaneous nephrostomy tubes placed during 52 pregnancies from 2008 to 2018.
finding: Percutaneous nephrostomy drainage is a safe and effective treatment for managing symptomatic hydronephrosis in pregnant patients, although it is less effective for pain relief when retrograde ureteral stents are already in place, and rapid encrustation requiring more frequent exchanges is common.
gest_age: Mean gestational age at PCN placement was 27 weeks (range, 8-36 weeks)
